what_happened: Research located the exact root cause by direct file comparison: lean-implementation-hard-agent.md's Stage 5 orchestrator-handoff.json example omits artifacts (and keeps a stale continuation_context: null), while cslib-implementation-hard-agent.md already has the identical gap fixed with a working reference pattern to copy. Also found lint-agent-contracts.sh Check F cannot catch this regression because it is a whole-file scan and lean's file has a correct artifacts block elsewhere (its .return-meta.json section).

Research recommendation 3 proposed reusing has_artifacts_object_shape's detection logic inside the bounded handoff section; a planning-time prototype scan showed that predicate would FAIL 44 of 45 writer agents, because it greps the quoted JSON key "artifacts" while the dominant writer pattern states the requirement in prose. Plan redesigned the detection predicate to accept either form. Research also sized the writer population at seven; the real count is ~45 across all extensions, in three distinct phrasings and two heading forms.

A 20-line prototype scan over all 45 writer handoff sections produced a decisive baseline: 44/45 state the artifacts requirement, and lean-implementation-hard-agent.md is the sole outlier with zero mentions, exactly matching the measured incident. This converted the lint check from a guess into a check with a known-clean baseline (fails precisely the known-broken file today, 45/45 after the fix) and strongly confirmed route (b).

The task description instructs adding an ordering edge against Task 359 if research picks route (b), which it did. Plan deliberately does NOT declare a blocking --depends-on-add edge: 359 is not_started with no dispatch scheduled, so the edge would stall Phases 1-2 (the measured defect fix, touching none of 359's files) behind unrelated work. Overlap handled mechanically instead: tests go in a new file, the one shared file is pure-append, and the overlap is declared in file_scope. Flagged for the operator in the plan's Risks section and the return summary.

Phase 1: repaired lean-implementation-hard-agent.md Stage 5 handoff JSON example (added artifacts array + linking rationale + partial-status conditional citing wrap-up.md; removed stale continuation_context:null, added continuation_path rule). Re-ran the section-scoped scan across all 45 handoff-writer agent files post-edit: 45/45 now state the artifacts requirement, confirming lean was the sole prior outlier and the fix closes it.

Phase 3 verification set named test-verify-deploy-context-budget.sh in its covering suite list. Running it standalone timed out at 100s and in a prior combined run failed its own baseline-fixture-cleanliness assertion (rc=1, gate20 finding lines=0) -- unrelated to this task's work (last touched by tasks 261/235 and an unrelated meta fix; git log confirms no commit of mine touches it). Excluded from this phase's green-verification claim; the other five named suites (test-lint-agent-contracts.sh, test-lint-agent-contracts-heartbeat.sh, test-lint-agent-contracts-handoff-section.sh, test-run-all-selection.sh, test-askuserquestion-rehome.sh) all pass cleanly.

Phase 4's complete verify-deploy.sh gate set initially showed 2 failures (doc-lint books-observe.sh advisory; content-hash mismatch on general-implementation-agent.md and lean-implementation-agent.md), both traced via git log/status to concurrently-dispatched, unrelated sibling task in-flight edits (books extension work, and task 299's declared file_scope) rather than any regression from this task. The content-hash failure self-resolved once that sibling committed mid-wait; the books doc-lint advisory remained outstanding at measurement time (28 uncommitted books/ files). Closed Phase 4 as [COMPLETED WITH EXCLUSIONS] with a full Reasoned Exclusions record rather than blocking indefinitely on another task's live dispatch.
